meta.title: Durable send, acknowledgement and asynchronous outbox

messages.label: Locked head; sender/client-ID lookup
messages.note: Existing identical send returns its committed result; conflict returns 409.

messages.label: New ID: message + next sequence + outbox
BEGIN; claim pending row: SKIP LOCKED
On publish success: mark published; COMMIT
messages.note: Crash before mark commits can repeat the hint.

messages.label: Conversation hint (can repeat or be missed)
Subscribed feed: committed head, tail, receipts
Ordered WS events through Nginx
messages.note: Server cursor advances on enqueue; device advances after its callback.

cards.title: Durability boundary
items: Message, last_sequence and outbox share one PostgreSQL transaction.
No successful new-send response precedes COMMIT; Redis is not on the acknowledgement path.
Commit uncertainty or a lost response: retry the same sender/client ID.
ACK and publishing can race after commit; ACK-first here is one possible interleaving.

cards.title: Publisher failure behavior
items: Each app has one publisher; SKIP LOCKED coordinates them through PostgreSQL.
Its claim transaction stays open across the bounded Redis call.
Publish failure rolls back; retry backoff is bounded by 5 s.
Publish accepted with no subscribers is not delivery proof; repeated publication is safe.

cards.title: Receiving side
items: Receiver was already authenticated, membership-checked and subscribed.
Redis listener targets one shared conversation feed; four local workers refresh feeds.
One-second server reconciliation repairs lost hints; old cursors use authorized history.
Client suppresses duplicates and accepts only contiguous sequence after callback success.

cards.title: Limits and scope
items: One PostgreSQL and one Redis instance; application replication is not dependency HA.
128-event queues and five-second writes bound slow consumers; reconnect recovers durable history.
Reads/receipt updates are separate HTTP operations, not automatic message acknowledgements.
Nginx forwards ingress/egress and is omitted as a participant; positions show order, not measured timing.
